theme: Common design patterns in iOS code: singleton, factory method and adapter pattern

terms.definition: A class that has exactly one shared instance for the whole app.

terms.definition: A method that creates and returns objects so the caller skips the initializer.

terms.definition: A pattern that wraps an object so it fits the interface another part expects.

video.description:
Learn to explain three classic design patterns: Singleton, Factory Method & Adapter Pattern, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Singleton - A class that has exactly one shared instance for the whole app.
Factory Method - A method that creates and returns objects so the caller skips the initializer.
Adapter Pattern - A pattern that wraps an object so it fits the interface another part expects.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

Explain Singleton, Factory Method & Adapter Pattern in iOS by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
Singleton, Factory Method, Adapter Pattern 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Singleton - A class that has exactly one shared instance for the whole app.
한국어: Singleton: 앱 전체에서 공유 인스턴스가 딱 하나뿐인 클래스

Factory Method - A method that creates and returns objects so the caller skips the initializer.
한국어: Factory Method: 호출하는 쪽이 이니셜라이저를 쓰지 않도록 객체를 만들어 돌려주는 메서드

Adapter Pattern - A pattern that wraps an object so it fits the interface another part expects.
한국어: Adapter Pattern: 다른 쪽이 기대하는 인터페이스에 맞게 객체를 감싸는 패턴

landscape.hook: Can you explain Singleton, Factory Method and Adapter Pattern in English?

dialogue.title: Shared everywhere

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, I found `Settings.shared` all over our code. Is it a singleton?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. A singleton has exactly one shared instance for the whole app.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It is easy to use, but it hides dependencies and makes tests hard. Use it carefully.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Okay. What about creating many objects with different setups?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use a factory method. It creates and returns the object, so callers skip the initializer.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Like a function that returns a new object?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, that is a factory method. The type picks the right setup.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And the old SDK has a different interface than our code.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then write an adapter. The adapter pattern wraps the old object so it fits your protocol.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the adapter pattern changes the interface but not the work?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. And do not replace one singleton with another singleton.
The settings object is a singleton, so avoid changing it in tests.
